plan.title: Differential expression between conditions
plan.analytical_narrative: No dataset facts were available at planning time (the profile was still being built), so the plan is deliberately generic and makes the executing agent confirm the data type, the condition variable, the replicate structure and the organism before fitting any model. Step 1 does the QC and a count-appropriate differential expression fit and writes the full result tables. Step 2 interprets the DE results with pathway enrichment against hallmark gene sets, only if the organism is human. The DE step carries the answer to the research question on its own. If the design turns out to be unanswerable (no replicates, or condition fully confounded with batch), step 1 must stop and say so rather than report p-values.

steps.name: Differential expression between conditions
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the conditions in the input expression data?
steps.description: Read the expression input and its sample metadata. Identify the condition variable(s), the replicate counts per group, and any batch or covariate columns. Run sample-level QC (library size or total signal, low-expression filtering, sample-correlation/PCA to spot outliers and batch effects). Fit a differential expression model that matches the data type. For raw counts use DESeq2 (with apeglm LFC shrinkage) or edgeR; for log-scale normalised microarray or other continuous data use limma. Include batch or other covariates in the design when they are not collinear with condition. If there are more than two conditions, test the contrasts that the metadata support and state which contrasts were run. Report for each contrast: log2 fold change, standard error or shrunken LFC, test statistic, raw p-value and FDR-adjusted p-value, for all tested genes. Call genes significant at FDR < 0.05 and report the |log2FC| cutoff, if one is used, separately. Produce a volcano plot, an MA plot, a PCA plot coloured by condition, and a heatmap of the top DE genes. Write the full results table and the significant-gene table as CSV files.
acceptance_criteria: The data type, the condition variable and its levels, and the sample count per group are stated explicitly
The statistical method matches the data type (count-based model for raw counts, limma for continuous normalised data)
Full per-gene results with raw p-value and FDR are written for every contrast tested
The number of significant up- and down-regulated genes at FDR < 0.05 is reported for each contrast
QC plots (PCA, sample correlation or equivalent) and volcano/MA plots are produced
constraints: Do not invent conditions or sample labels; derive them from the supplied metadata or file headers
If any group of a comparison has no replicate, or condition is fully confounded with batch, stop and report that the contrast cannot be tested, instead of reporting p-values
Never apply a count-based model to data that are already log-transformed or normalised; do not re-normalise normalised data
Use FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg) adjustment across all tested genes, and report the filtering rule applied before testing
caveats: Small group sizes give low power; say so in the summary
Gene identifiers may be Ensembl IDs or symbols; if Ensembl IDs are used, map them to symbols with the gene annotation reference if one is available, and keep the original IDs in the output
Check the sign convention of the log2 fold change (which condition is the reference) and state it

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among the genes that differ between the conditions?
steps.description: Using the ranked full per-gene results from the DE step, run pre-ranked gene set enrichment (fgsea) on the hallmark gene sets for the organism of the data, plus an over-representation test on the significant up and down gene lists separately if there are enough genes. Hallmark gene sets and KEGG pathway gene sets are the reference collections needed. First confirm that the organism of the data is human and that a gene-symbol mapping exists; the available hallmark and KEGG collections are human only. If the organism is not human, or the genes cannot be mapped to symbols, do not use the human sets directly. Report this limitation and finish with the DE result alone, or use msigdbr for the right species if it holds it. Report NES, p-value and FDR for each set, and plot the top enriched sets.
acceptance_criteria: The organism and the gene-set collection used are stated, and they match
Enrichment tables with NES and FDR are written for each contrast
A plot of the top enriched gene sets is produced, or a clear note explains why enrichment was skipped
constraints: Rank genes by a signed statistic (for example the DE test statistic) and not by p-value alone
Do not run human gene sets on non-human data without an orthology mapping
caveats: Enrichment is exploratory and depends on the quality of the DE result; with few DE genes the over-representation test is underpowered

results.text:
I submitted a two-step plan, and the plan was accepted. It is generic because no dataset facts were available. The data profile was still being built and the profile and file-listing tools were unavailable. I did not invent conditions, organism, or data type.

- **T1S1, differential expression:** The step first confirms the data type, the condition variable and its levels, the replicates per group, and any batch columns. It then does QC and fits a model that matches the data:
  - DESeq2 with apeglm shrinkage, or edgeR, for raw counts.
  - limma for normalised continuous data.

  It reports log2 fold change, raw p-value and FDR (BH) for every gene in every contrast, and calls significance at FDR < 0.05. It also writes volcano, MA, PCA and heatmap plots and the result tables. If a group has no replicate, or condition is fully confounded with batch, the step stops and says so instead of reporting p-values.
- **T1S2, pathway enrichment:** This step depends on T1S1. It runs pre-ranked fgsea on the hallmark and KEGG gene sets, which are human-only in this environment. If the data are not human, or the genes can't be mapped to symbols, it skips enrichment and reports why. The differential expression answer does not depend on this step.

If you can tell me the organism, the data type (raw counts or normalised), and which conditions to compare, I can replace the generic wording with a plan that names them.
